_comment: Draft conversations use the existing speaker/portrait/lines schema. Physical repairs rescues landings fights pumps and finale resolution are never auto-completed by speech. Event guards are recorded in water_characters.json and require parent integration.

water_mara_pre.speaker: Dockkeeper Mara
lines: The tall white falls beyond the islands are the Veilfall. Keep them in sight; every troubled channel here leads back there.
Reedhaven is your first stop. Its departure pier is broken, but the sheltered swimming channel reaches their near shore.
Before you leave, find Pell by the calm inlet and prepare food at camp. A short crossing still deserves a return plan.

water_mara_post.speaker: Dockkeeper Mara
lines: The first civilian supplies reached Shellwatch this morning. I finally took the barricade chalk off my dock board.
Reedhaven's crews, Shellwatch's families and Salt Crown's traders can share the docks again.
Rodfolk and Cloudreach couriers are carrying medicine and blankets without a Tether permit.
The sea still has currents. Rest and choose your landing even when nobody is using the water against you.
Your road home starts at the First Shore passage to Stormwood. The return gates lead through Cloudreach to the Meadows.

water_pell_pre.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: Start where you can still put your feet down. Pick the far landing before you leave this bank.
Swimming spends stamina. If you run out, you begin losing health; reach shallow ground immediately instead of waiting in deep water.
Practice the sheltered inlet yourself. Hearing this lesson does not prove that you can make the crossing.

water_pell_post.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: I saw you come back through the inlet. The route feels smaller once you know where the ground rises.
Keep teaching the new arrivals that stopping in deep water does not refill their strength.

water_elin_pre.speaker: Campkeeper Elin
lines: Leave your wet boots by the fire. There is room for the whole team to recover before you travel.
Food helps you prepare; a low stomach is a soft setback, not a death sentence. Your swimming stamina is the urgent thing out there.
Use the camp and check each creature's health. Carry a revive where you can find it when a crossing goes wrong.

water_elin_post.speaker: Campkeeper Elin
lines: The camp is busy with returning families now. Nobody has to sleep beside a closed departure gate.
I kept your usual place near the fire. A victory is a good reason to look after the team that earned it.

water_rowan_pre.speaker: Pierwright Rowan
lines: The far pier needs reed fiber and driftwood. Gather the repair materials, then work at the damaged supports.
I can explain the repair, but I cannot nail a board down by talking to you. The work site is beside the broken railing.
The reeds grow along the sheltered bank; use the dry route between patches so gathering does not empty your stamina.

water_rowan_post.speaker: Pierwright Rowan
lines: The repaired pier carries people again. I saved the old broken plank to remind myself what a proper landing is worth.
Now that the pumps are quiet, we can repair the smaller paths instead of constantly rebuilding this one.

water_sella_pre.speaker: Caretaker Sella
lines: Mosshell rests near gentle banks. Give one space and it will usually let you pass without a fight.
You can own five creatures in total. If you want a new companion, think about who already travels with you.
A water creature is not automatically a swim mount. The saddle needs a species that can safely carry you.

water_sella_post.speaker: Caretaker Sella
lines: The shore creatures have returned to their old resting places. They no longer crowd the one calm corner of the marsh.
A familiar Mosshell can carry the next expedition as faithfully as an Alpha, once you have the Swim Stone and saddle.

water_tovin_pre.speaker: Keeper Tovin
lines: This pier opens onto an exposed channel. I ask travelers to show that their team can handle pressure before they depart.
Our battle stays on these broad terraces. Watch which creature I send first, and keep room to move around its charge.
Winning the demonstration opens the departure route; speaking with me does not. Prepare before you challenge me.

water_tovin_post.speaker: Keeper Tovin
lines: You earned the pier fairly. I will keep the training space open for anyone who wants a safer first expedition.
The channel is calmer after your victory at the Veilfall, but learning to read a charge is still useful.

water_adair_pre.speaker: Surveyor Adair
lines: See the foam moving past the rocks? That is the direction the current will carry your body.
The sheltered line takes longer on the map but pushes against you less. Compare your landing options, not just the straight distance.
Mark a safe landing by reaching it yourself. A drawing from this terrace cannot tell us whether its bank is climbable.

water_adair_post.speaker: Surveyor Adair
lines: Your landing notes have made a practical route guide. People can choose the sheltered line before they enter the water.
The strongest current has shifted since the pumps stopped. The foam tells the new truth; an old chart does not.

water_nalia_pre.speaker: Resident Nalia
lines: Team Tether pushed us away from the usable pier. Our neighbors are stranded beyond their patrol and the pump controls.
Clear a route to the residents and shut the pump down at its switch. We need both before this becomes a safe departure.
The camp is on the raised shore. Bring injured creatures there before you try the channel toward Tidal Cradle.

water_nalia_post.speaker: Resident Nalia
lines: Everyone from our dock is accounted for. I wrote their names on the camp board and crossed out nobody.
We are keeping the old patrol shelter for travelers. It feels better with blankets where the warning signs used to hang.

water_bren_pre.speaker: Pump Tender Bren
lines: I maintained that pump before Tether fenced it off. The intake pulls loose water toward their marked channel.
Find the control beside the machinery after the approach is safe. Do not send your own body into the intake.
A stopped pump changes the route, but you still need enough stamina to reach the next bank.

water_bren_post.speaker: Pump Tender Bren
lines: Listen to that: waves on stone instead of an engine fighting them. I had forgotten this shore's ordinary sound.
I am turning the spare housing into a dry store. Machinery should help the settlement, not hold it hostage.

water_iona_pre.speaker: Researcher Iona
lines: Aquaryn uses both the shore and the surface channel. Watch where its sweep ends before you rush its flank.
Defeat Aquaryn or catch it to settle the trial. Either victory opens the way to Salt Crown.
Follow the stone-and-torch shoals along the sheltered crossing. Rest on each dry centre before the next swim. Your Swim Stone also unlocks my optional saddle lesson.

water_iona_post.speaker: Researcher Iona
lines: The way to Salt Crown is open. Keep the companions you know; the marked shoals give you places to rest between swims.
If you would like to ride a compatible swimmer, keep its saddle in your bag and use its Ride prompt. Watch its stamina as carefully as your own.

water_otto_pre.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: Your five can stay together all the way to the Veilfall. Follow the sheltered crossings and rest on the dry stone-and-torch shoals.
A Mosshell or Riverdrake can make those crossings quicker if you already travel with one. Riding needs a Swim Stone and Swim Saddle.
Iona teaches the saddle pattern. Gather reed fiber and driftwood, and mine Reef Stone if you choose to craft it.

water_otto_post.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: I watched a traveler leave on a Mosshell today. Slow, steady, and enough strength left to enjoy the landing.
The shoals are there for swimmers too. Set your own pace, and keep enough strength to reach the next dry landing.

water_edda_pre.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: Salt Crown is the last full settlement before the occupied channels. Rest here and look at the crossing ahead with a fresh team.
Our realm keeps the Tideglass Compass. Its blessing is Tidal Guard, and it belongs in the same single active power choice as your other relics.
The Deep Watcher is held beneath the Veilfall. Freeing it must come before any offer of companionship.

water_edda_post.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: The Compass marks a realm that can breathe again. Carry it home and place it at its stone in the Meadows shrine circle when you are ready.
Only one relic power can be active. Choosing Tidal Guard is a choice about preparation, not a second power hidden underneath the first.

water_corin_pre.speaker: Defector Corin
lines: The outer pumps feed the crystal behind the Veilfall. Nerissa calls the current network a road, but she decides who gets to use it.
On Sluice Isle, one control sits behind the patrol and another routes the channel. You need both to prepare the last approach.
From below, the stronghold looks like a mountain and a waterfall. Follow the hike; the entrance is behind the falling water.

water_corin_post.speaker: Defector Corin
lines: I told people where the controls were. You were the one who reached them. I will spend the next season helping repair what I helped build.
The channel network is quiet now. Nobody should need my old uniform to reach their own home.

water_orsen_pre.speaker: Channel Keeper Orsen
lines: The patrol control and the channel-routing switch do different jobs. Clearing only one leaves the preparation channel unsafe.
Read the visible flow before operating the sluice. Use the raised path to reach the switch instead of fighting the intake.
Rest at the camp before leaving Sluice Isle. Take the sheltered shoals one at a time, and recover on dry ground.
Beyond the reef off this isle lies Deep Watch. Tidecoil hunts its reef edge, and while it does nobody can chart that island's current home.
It is optional water, and dangerous. Go only with a rested team and a way back.

water_orsen_post.speaker: Channel Keeper Orsen
lines: The two controls now serve the landing instead of the barricade. We can keep the shelter supplied from Salt Crown.
I still check the raised paths each morning. A freed channel deserves maintenance as much as a guarded one did.
Deep Watch is still out past the reef. Tidecoil did not leave with the Tether; if you want that return current charted, settle it first.

water_orsen_deep_watch_chart_lead.speaker: Channel Keeper Orsen
lines: The reef edge at Deep Watch has gone quiet. With Tidecoil settled, the return current finally runs in a line you can read.
There is a chart table beside the Deep Watch landing. Mark the eddy there yourself; one honest reading gives every swimmer a shorter way back.
And the cache on the lookout that Tidecoil kept everyone away from is reachable now. Whoever made the crossing should take what is theirs.

water_orsen_deep_watch_charted.speaker: Channel Keeper Orsen
lines: You charted the Deep Watch eddy. I can see the calm line from the landing now; I will add it to the keepers' map.
That was the optional water. The patrol control and the channel-routing switch here still need doing before the last approach is safe.

water_orsen_post_charted.speaker: Channel Keeper Orsen
lines: The two controls now serve the landing instead of the barricade, and the Deep Watch eddy you charted runs calm all the way back.
I still check the raised paths each morning. A freed channel deserves maintenance as much as a guarded one did.

water_jessa_pre.speaker: Courier Jessa
lines: I turned back from the Veilfall once with my mount shaking. Turning back early was the reason we both reached this camp.
Check your stamina, health and supplies. If you are riding, check your companion too; an exhausted mount can leave you swimming.
After both controls are quiet, follow the sheltered shoals to Veilfall. Rest on dry land between swims, then take the mountain path to the falls.

water_jessa_post.speaker: Courier Jessa
lines: My first delivery through the restored channel was blankets. After all those supply manifests, that felt like an excellent cargo.
The way is open, but the distance has not disappeared. I still stop here before I cross.

water_halen_pre.speaker: Campkeeper Halen
lines: You have reached the foot of the Veilfall. Rest before the hike; the waterfall hides the entrance higher on the mountain.
Officer Venn holds the approach. Beyond him are the wet caves, pumps, sluice bridge and the Heart Chamber.
Bring a team ready to move between raised safe ground and the discharge lanes. The human never needs to attack the machinery.

water_halen_post.speaker: Campkeeper Halen
lines: The waterfall sounds different with the pump chambers quiet behind it. The path is still steep, so take the descent carefully.
This camp will stay open. People should get to visit the mountain without preparing for a siege.

water_venn_pre.speaker: Officer Venn
lines: You followed the service channels all the way here. The waterfall was supposed to keep the gate out of sight.
My creatures hold this approach. You will have to beat them before you reach the passage behind the water.
Watch the footing. Even a trained team loses control when its trainer ignores where the next exchange will happen.

water_venn_post.speaker: Officer Venn
lines: The gate is open. Nerissa's orders were clear; they were not worth what those orders did to the islands.
I will leave the approach clear while the residents recover the pump equipment.

water_nerissa_pre.speaker: Captain Nerissa
lines: These channels connected scattered islands into one network. I built a system that answered to a single command.
Your creature can challenge mine, but read the discharge lanes. The raised platforms will not protect a careless approach forever.
My team stands between you and the tether. You will have to defeat us before you can release the Deep Watcher.

water_nerissa_post.speaker: Captain Nerissa
lines: The crystal is quiet. Every channel I called mine is moving without my permission.
The Deep Watcher is no longer contained here. I cannot pretend the islands needed its captivity after what you have shown them.

water_trainer_pell_trial_intro.speaker: Pell
lines: Try reading the opening splash before you close the distance.

water_trainer_pell_trial_win.speaker: Pell
lines: You left room for the second attack. That is the habit I wanted to see.

water_trainer_pell_trial_lose.speaker: Pell
lines: A quick step inward is tempting. Watch the space where the next splash will land.

water_trainer_fen_intro.speaker: Fen
lines: This sheltered cove leaves room to practice a flanking team.

water_trainer_fen_win.speaker: Fen
lines: You kept both exits in view. My flank never became a trap.

water_trainer_fen_lose.speaker: Fen
lines: You followed my first retreat. Next time keep the bank behind you open.

water_trainer_lysa_intro.speaker: Lysa
lines: This repair pier is closed under channel authority.

water_trainer_lysa_win.speaker: Lysa
lines: The pier crew can pass. I will not make them fight again.

water_trainer_lysa_lose.speaker: Lysa
lines: Your first attack met the shell. Try reaching its side after the commitment.

water_trainer_daro_intro.speaker: Daro
lines: My pair rushes hard but has to recover. Can you find that moment?

water_trainer_daro_win.speaker: Daro
lines: You waited out the rush. They had nowhere useful to put the next one.

water_trainer_daro_lose.speaker: Daro
lines: I caught you moving straight backward. Leave the charge lane sooner.

water_trainer_tovin_intro.speaker: Keeper Tovin
lines: Show me a team that can adapt when a steady defender gives way to a fast flanker.

water_trainer_tovin_win.speaker: Keeper Tovin
lines: You adapted. The demonstration is complete and the departure pier is yours to use.

water_trainer_tovin_lose.speaker: Keeper Tovin
lines: Your team can recover here. Think about which creature should face my second one.

water_trainer_keir_intro.speaker: Keir
lines: Two patient defenders. You do not need to hurry into either shell.

water_trainer_keir_win.speaker: Keir
lines: You made me turn before committing. That broke my defense.

water_trainer_keir_lose.speaker: Keir
lines: I can wait longer than you can trade careless hits. Make me move.

water_trainer_rune_intro.speaker: Rune
lines: The bird draws your attention while the seal changes the range.

water_trainer_rune_win.speaker: Rune
lines: You respected both ranges. My team never found a free approach.

water_trainer_rune_lose.speaker: Rune
lines: Watch the creature in front of you rather than preparing for the one still waiting.

water_trainer_solm_intro.speaker: Solm
lines: Those residents stay behind our line until this dock is secure.

water_trainer_solm_win.speaker: Solm
lines: Our line is broken. Take them to the raised shore.

water_trainer_solm_lose.speaker: Solm
lines: You stayed in front of Mirejaw too long. Its patience is the danger.

water_trainer_irva_intro.speaker: Irva
lines: The pump controls are behind me. A conversation will not stop the intake.

water_trainer_irva_win.speaker: Irva
lines: I cannot hold the controls. Shut them down yourself if that is your plan.

water_trainer_irva_lose.speaker: Irva
lines: My charge moved you away from the switch. Settle the fight before approaching it.

water_trainer_nel_intro.speaker: Nel
lines: The camp is close enough for a practice match. Let us test your recovery discipline.

water_trainer_nel_win.speaker: Nel
lines: You finished with options left. That matters before a swim.

water_trainer_nel_lose.speaker: Nel
lines: Recover at camp and change the matchup before you try again.

water_trainer_oswin_intro.speaker: Oswin
lines: The research path is restricted. Your team will have to clear it.

water_trainer_oswin_win.speaker: Oswin
lines: The path is clear. Aquaryn beyond it is no creature of ours.

water_trainer_oswin_lose.speaker: Oswin
lines: You chased Riverdrake into Mirejaw's preferred reach. Read the next matchup.

water_trainer_tal_intro.speaker: Tal
lines: A slow team can finish a long expedition. See whether you can move mine.

water_trainer_tal_win.speaker: Tal
lines: You made patience work for you instead of against you.

water_trainer_tal_lose.speaker: Tal
lines: Bring pressure from another angle. Hitting the strongest point is expensive.

water_trainer_sera_intro.speaker: Sera
lines: Salt Crown's supplies follow our routing orders.

water_trainer_sera_win.speaker: Sera
lines: The supply landing is open. Your people can use it.

water_trainer_sera_lose.speaker: Sera
lines: You let the runner set every exchange. Take back the space between attacks.

water_trainer_odan_intro.speaker: Odan
lines: Fast travel and fast combat ask different things from the same team.

water_trainer_odan_win.speaker: Odan
lines: You handled the change of pace. Your mount is more than a crossing tool.

water_trainer_odan_lose.speaker: Odan
lines: Keep enough space for the seal before preparing for the drake's rush.

water_trainer_yara_intro.speaker: Yara
lines: These ruins reward a patient approach. My team will test whether you kept that patience.

water_trainer_yara_win.speaker: Yara
lines: You found the openings without giving up your escape route.

water_trainer_yara_lose.speaker: Yara
lines: Rest on the landing before trying again. The return swim is still ahead of you.

water_trainer_bex_intro.speaker: Bex
lines: The patrol control answers to this post.

water_trainer_bex_win.speaker: Bex
lines: The post is yours. The second channel control is a separate job.

water_trainer_bex_lose.speaker: Bex
lines: You tried to break the shell head on. Reposition after its attack.

water_trainer_calder_intro.speaker: Calder
lines: You reached one control. My team holds the route to the other.

water_trainer_calder_win.speaker: Calder
lines: Both approaches are open now. Operate the channel control yourself.

water_trainer_calder_lose.speaker: Calder
lines: You handled the first charge and missed the second. Keep watching the send-outs.

water_trainer_vera_intro.speaker: Vera
lines: This raised platform is wide enough for an honest test of ranged pressure.

water_trainer_vera_win.speaker: Vera
lines: You crossed the danger space at the right moment.

water_trainer_vera_lose.speaker: Vera
lines: A ranged attack still has recovery. Use it instead of trading from the same spot.

water_trainer_tess_intro.speaker: Tess
lines: The named apex lies farther along the current. Check your team's readiness here first.

water_trainer_tess_win.speaker: Tess
lines: Your team kept its shape. Keep some recovery supplies for Tidecoil.

water_trainer_tess_lose.speaker: Tess
lines: This is a good place to turn back and prepare. Pride does not shorten the crossing.

water_trainer_fennel_intro.speaker: Fennel
lines: The lower hike is part of the captain's perimeter.

water_trainer_fennel_win.speaker: Fennel
lines: You have the trail. Venn holds the waterfall approach above.

water_trainer_fennel_lose.speaker: Fennel
lines: You watched the falls instead of the battle. Give this exchange your full attention.

water_trainer_venn_intro.speaker: Officer Venn
lines: The concealed gate opens only when my team can no longer hold it.

water_trainer_venn_win.speaker: Officer Venn
lines: The approach is lost. The passage behind the falls is clear.

water_trainer_venn_lose.speaker: Officer Venn
lines: Recover below before returning. The wet-cave fight beyond me will ask more of you.

water_trainer_morra_intro.speaker: Morra
lines: The sluice bridge feeds the Heart Chamber. You will go no farther.

water_trainer_morra_win.speaker: Morra
lines: The bridge is clear. Watch the discharge lanes beyond it.

water_trainer_morra_lose.speaker: Morra
lines: You let the narrow approach choose your footing. Use the raised space.

water_trainer_evi_intro.speaker: Evi
lines: One last practice match at the safe camp, if your team needs it.

water_trainer_evi_win.speaker: Evi
lines: You kept a healthy answer for the final defender.

water_trainer_evi_lose.speaker: Evi
lines: There is time to rest. A practice loss should teach you before the chamber does.

water_trainer_nerissa_intro.speaker: Captain Nerissa
lines: My team and the channel network hold this chamber. Read both if you mean to break through.

water_trainer_nerissa_win.speaker: Captain Nerissa
lines: The network is finished. The crystal can no longer hold the Deep Watcher.

water_trainer_nerissa_lose.speaker: Captain Nerissa
lines: You treated the lanes as scenery. Watch the warning and move your creature onto safe ground.

water_pell_lesson_briefing.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: Pick the sheltered landing and watch your stamina while you cross.

lines.text: I have explained the route. Now practice in the inlet; the crossing itself is what counts.

water_iona_recipe.speaker: Researcher Iona
lines: For riding, the Swim Stone lets you learn this saddle pattern: eight reed fiber, six driftwood and four reefstone.

lines.text: Here is the pattern. Craft it at Tidal Cradle’s camp workbench. Keep the saddle in your bag, bring out a compatible companion, and use its Ride prompt.

water_iona_attunement.speaker: Researcher Iona
lines: Aquaryn's trial is already over; Salt Crown's crossing is open to you. I can also attune your Swim Stone if you would like to learn to ride.

lines.text: Stand with me at the cradle. I will attune a Swim Stone to you from the trial's shared wake; it can be granted only once.

water_edda_guardian_offer.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: The Deep Watcher is free. If you invite it into your team, the five-creature limit still applies.

lines.text: Consider the companions already beside you. The ceremony lets you decide. If you would rather not, decline beside the Guardian: that answer is final for you in this world, and it does not undo the freedom you won.

water_edda_guardian_neutral.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: The Deep Watcher is free of the crystal. Its offer belongs to those who stood against Nerissa beneath the Veilfall, and each of them answers it once.
Nothing more is asked of you at the chamber. Rest here before you go on.

water_pell_lantern_lead.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: You made the inlet. Now look west, past the point: that dark rock arch standing out of the water is Lantern Cove.
Under the arch there is a dry nook the old lamp-keepers used. Something is still tucked in there, and nobody has swum out for it in years.
Take the sheltered line along the shallows, not the open water. Then come back here and tell me how the swim home felt. The return is the part worth learning.

water_pell_lantern_reminder.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: Lantern Cove is west of the point; you can see the arch from the beach. Follow the shallows and rest on dry ground before you turn back.
The cache is in the dry nook under the arch. Come and tell me about the swim back once you have it.

water_pell_lantern_return.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: You went under the arch and came back on your own strength. That is the whole lesson, done properly.
The swim back is always longer than it looks from the cove. Now you know where the shallows break and where to stop.
Keep whatever you found in the nook; it was left for whoever made that crossing. I will tell the next swimmer the line you took.

water_pell_lantern_thanks.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: The Lantern Cove line is on my board now. Two new arrivals made it out to the arch and back this morning.
Whenever you pass the point, remember the shallows run closest on the way home.

water_pell_post_lantern.speaker: Swimmer Pell
lines: The currents feel gentler everywhere now. Even the Lantern Cove line you charted is an easy swim for the new arrivals.
Keep teaching them that stopping in deep water does not refill their strength.

water_adair_gull_lead.speaker: Surveyor Adair
lines: See the foam moving past the rocks? That is the direction the current will carry your body. The sheltered line takes longer but pushes against you less.
My survey partner was stranded on Gull Rest, the gull-cliff island off Reedhaven's west shore. The boats brought her home, but her satchel of current readings stayed on the upper slope.
If you take Reedhaven's sheltered crossing out there, bring the observations back through Brine Steps. With them I can chart a safe line to Gull Rest for everyone.

water_adair_gull_reminder.speaker: Surveyor Adair
lines: Gull Rest is reached from Reedhaven. Keep to the sheltered line and rest where your feet touch.
The satchel should be on the slope above the landing. Bring it back through here when you next pass Brine Steps.

water_adair_gull_return.speaker: Surveyor Adair
lines: That is her satchel. Look at these readings: she timed the eddies around Gull Rest every hour for three days.
The sheltered crossing holds steady even when the tide turns. I can mark it as safe, landing to landing.
Whatever else she left on that slope is yours to keep. The observations belong on the survey board.

water_adair_gull_thanks.speaker: Surveyor Adair
lines: The Gull Rest route is charted now: sheltered line from Reedhaven, rest at the shallows, land below the cliff.
Mark a safe landing by reaching it yourself. A drawing from this terrace cannot tell us whether its bank is climbable.

water_adair_post_gull.speaker: Surveyor Adair
lines: Your landing notes and the Gull Rest readings have made a practical route guide. People choose the sheltered line before they enter the water.
The strongest current has shifted since the pumps stopped. The charted Gull Rest route still holds; the foam tells the new truth.

water_otto_nest_lead.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: Your five can stay together all the way to the Veilfall. Follow the sheltered crossings and rest on the dry stone-and-torch shoals.
If you ever want a swimmer to carry you, start with the shell nest on this island's upper slope. It stays dry at every tide, and the rock there is good Reef Stone.
Mine it with a pickaxe, then come and find me. Bring a swimmer of your own, or come once Aquaryn's trial is settled, whichever way it goes. I will show you where the gentle ones live.

water_otto_nest_reminder.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: The shell nest is up the slope from here, above the tideline. Look for the exposed Reef Stone.
You do not need Aquaryn for any of this. Mine the stone, and we will talk about swimmers.

water_otto_nest_wait.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: Good stone from the nest. Keep it; a saddle frame needs every piece.
A saddle still needs a swimmer under it. Come back with one of your own, or once Aquaryn's trial is settled either way, and I will tell you where to look.

water_otto_nest_return.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: You found the nest and kept the stone. Here, berries from the cradle garden, for whoever carries you across.
If you want another swimmer: Mosshell graze the shallows on this island, Riverdrake hunt the channel around Shellwatch, and Sirenseal bask off Salt Crown and the Drowned Garden.
Iona teaches the saddle pattern. Any of them will carry you once it is fitted; none of them needs to be Aquaryn.

water_otto_nest_thanks.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: Mosshell on Tidal Cradle's shallows, Riverdrake by Shellwatch, Sirenseal off Salt Crown. The nest's stone is for your saddle.
Set your own pace, and keep enough strength to reach the next dry landing.

water_otto_post_nest.speaker: Tracker Otto
lines: I watched a traveler leave on a Mosshell today. Slow, steady, and enough strength left to enjoy the landing.
The shell nest is quiet now the currents have calmed. Swimmers still gather where I showed you.

water_edda_garden_lead.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: Salt Crown is the last full settlement before the occupied channels. Our realm keeps the Tideglass Compass; its blessing is Tidal Guard, one choice among your relic powers.
The Deep Watcher is held beneath the Veilfall. Freeing it must come before any offer of companionship.
Before you go on: east of here, the Drowned Garden's old vault still stands above the water. You can see its wall from our terrace.
The keepers carved the dock accounts into that wall long before Team Tether came. Copy what is written there and bring it to me; our own records burned.

water_edda_garden_reminder.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: The vault is on the Drowned Garden, east of Salt Crown, above the waterline. Take the lawful route; no one needs to dive for it.
Rest here before you cross. The Compass and the Deep Watcher will wait for a fresh team.

water_edda_garden_return.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: You copied the whole wall. Here: the dock tallies, landing by landing, and the names of the keepers who kept them.
Before Team Tether, every dock was a shared landing. Each island kept its own mooring and answered to no one; the crossings were charted together each spring.
The Tether never built those docks. It barricaded them, and called the barricades order. This account proves the landings were always ours to share.
Keep what you found in the vault. The account belongs in Salt Crown's records, where anyone can read it.

water_edda_garden_thanks.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: The vault account sits with our records now. The dockkeepers come to read their grandparents' names.
Rest here and look at the crossing ahead with a fresh team.

water_edda_post_garden.speaker: Shrinekeeper Edda
lines: The Compass marks a realm that can breathe again. Carry it home and place it at its stone in the Meadows shrine circle when you are ready.
The docks are shared landings again, as the vault account says they always were.

water_halen_shelter_lead.speaker: Campkeeper Halen
lines: You have reached the foot of the Veilfall. Rest before the hike; the waterfall hides the entrance higher on the mountain, and Officer Venn holds the approach.
Before or after you face him, there is a sheltered way down beside Lastlight, my old lamp post, to the camp at the landing. The spray never reaches that hollow.
The creature bed there sits in the open. Bring 4 driftwood and 4 reed fiber to the camp and we can roof it for good, for anyone who comes through.
Then let one of your companions rest in it, and tell me whether it holds.

water_halen_shelter_reminder.speaker: Campkeeper Halen
lines: Follow the sheltered way beside Lastlight down to the landing camp. Leave 4 driftwood and 4 reed fiber at the bed.
There is driftwood along this shore. Keep enough for a saddle if you mean to ride; the shelter can wait for a spare armful.

water_halen_shelter_rest.speaker: Campkeeper Halen
lines: The roof is up over the landing bed. Let one of your companions rest there before the climb, or after it.
I want to know it keeps the spray off a real sleeper, not just an empty mattress.

water_halen_shelter_thanks.speaker: Campkeeper Halen
lines: Your companion slept dry under the new shelter. That bed stays sheltered for everyone who lands here.
Bring a team ready to move between raised safe ground and the discharge lanes. The human never needs to attack the machinery.

water_halen_post_shelter.speaker: Campkeeper Halen
lines: The waterfall sounds different with the pump chambers quiet behind it. The sheltered bed at the landing is full most nights now.
This camp will stay open. People should get to visit the mountain without preparing for a siege.
